mainTopic: How our משנה's praise of the virtuous fits רבי מאיר: the נדר/נדבה distinction, הלל הזקן's method for קרבנות, and שמעון הצדיק's view of נזירות taken purely for Heaven.
overview: The גמרא is trying to fit our משנה, which praises the virtuous for their offerings, with רבי מאיר, who says it is best not to vow at all. It answers that רבי מאיר only objected to a נדר, not a נדבה, and reads the משנה's word as 'volunteered' instead of 'vowed'. It then asks why a נדבה is any safer than a נדר. For קרבנות, the answer is the method of הלל הזקן: he made his animal holy only in the עזרה, right before slaughtering it, so no one could misuse it. For נזירות, the answer is that רבי מאיר follows שמעון הצדיק. שמעון הצדיק never ate an impure נזיר's אשם except once, when a handsome shepherd became a נזיר purely to break his own pride, and שמעון הצדיק praised him. רבי מני asks why only that אשם was avoided, and רבי יונה explains: an impure נזיר's term gets longer, so he may regret his נזירות, and his offerings become like חולין. A pure נזיר judged his own strength beforehand, so there is no such worry. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a second answer about which תנא the משנה follows, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר only objected to vows, not gift offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי מאיר's warning against vowing applies only to a נדר, not to a נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי מאיר said it is better not to vow, he meant a נדר. He did not say this about a נדבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering an earlier question: how can our משנה praise the virtuous for their offerings if רבי מאיר says it is best never to vow? It answers that רבי מאיר was only talking about a נדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדר and a נדבה are two different ways of promising a קרבן. רבי מאיר's warning covers only the נדר. So our משנה, which talks about the virtuous bringing נדבות, can fit his view.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow that puts an obligation on the person ('I take upon myself to bring an offering').
A gift offering, where a specific animal is set aside ('this animal is an offering').
When he said it (he only meant...)

steps.whyThisMatters: This נדר versus נדבה distinction is what the rest of this section is built on.

phrases.english: When Rabbi Meir said [that it is better not to vow],
he was talking about a vow;
about a gift offering he did not say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question of whether our משנה can follow רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a ruling (רבי מאיר speaks only about נדר).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's warning seemed to cover every kind of promise to bring a קרבן, which would clash with our משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר only discourages a נדר; a נדבה is fine.

steps.title: But the משנה uses the word 'vowed'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: our משנה itself says the person 'vowed' (נדר) to be a נזיר or bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches: if someone says 'like their נדבות', he has vowed to be a נזיר and to bring a קרבן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 1. The משנה's own wording says 'נדר', so it seems to be talking about a vow after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה describes the virtuous as making a נדר, then it clashes with רבי מאיר again. The distinction from step 1 does not seem to help, because the משנה uses the word for a vow.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is taught! (a challenge from a source)
Like their gift offerings (the virtuous people's).
A person who takes on נזירות: no wine, no haircut, no contact with the dead.

phrases.english: But it is taught [in our Mishnah]:
"Like their gift offerings" —
he has vowed regarding being a nazirite and bringing an offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 1 using the משנה's own words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that our משנה speaks only of נדבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says 'נדר', meaning a vow, which רבי מאיר discourages.

steps.title: Read the משנה as 'volunteered'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adjusts the wording of the משנה: read 'נדב' (volunteered) instead of 'נדר' (vowed).
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn the משנה as: he has volunteered to be a נזיר and to bring a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing one word in the משנה, from 'vowed' to 'volunteered'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the משנה is talking about a נדבה, which רבי מאיר does not discourage. So the משנה fits רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Teach it as... (the גמרא adjusts the wording of a source).
He volunteered or offered as a gift.

steps.confusionAlert: נדר (vowed) and נדב (volunteered) look and sound almost the same, but here they mean two different kinds of commitment.

phrases.english: Teach [the Mishnah as]:
he has volunteered regarding being a nazirite and bringing an offering.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Adjusting the wording of the source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says the virtuous made a נדר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה should read 'נדב': the virtuous make a נדבה.

steps.title: Why is a gift offering safer than a vow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if a נדר is avoided because of the risk of a stumbling block, a נדבה should be avoided too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is a vow different, that one should not make it, because maybe he will stumble with it? A נדבה should also be avoided, because maybe he will stumble with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the logic of step 1 itself. If the reason not to make a נדר is the fear of a תקלה, that same fear exists with a נדבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a נדר, the risk is that he will be slow to bring the קרבן. With a נדבה, the animal becomes holy right away, so someone might use it by mistake, which is the sin of מעילה. Either way, there is a risk.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
A stumbling block, meaning a chance to accidentally sin.
One who vows.

phrases.english: What is different about one who vows, that he should not [vow]?
Because perhaps he will come to a stumbling block with it?
A gift offering should also not [be given],
because perhaps he will come to a stumbling block with it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the distinction of step 1 and questions its logic.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between נדר and נדבה in רבי מאיר's view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason for avoiding a נדר (risk of תקלה) applies equally to a נדבה.

steps.title: הלל הזקן's method avoids the risk
steps.stepSummary: A נדבה can be given safely the way הלל הזקן did: making the animal holy only in the עזרה, right before slaughtering it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like הלל הזקן. A ברייתא teaches: they said about הלל הזקן that no one ever misused his עולה in his whole life. He would bring it to the עזרה while it was still ordinary (חולין), make it holy there, do סמיכה on it, and slaughter it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a נדבה can be done with no risk, and brings a ברייתא about הלל הזקן showing how.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The risk with a נדבה is that the animal is holy for a long time and someone might use it. הלל made it holy only at the last moment, so there was no time for anyone to misuse it. A נדר has no such fix, so the difference between them stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Hillel the Elder, the great sage.
Misused holy property for ordinary use (מעילה).
A burnt offering, burned entirely on the altar.
Ordinary, not holy.
The Temple courtyard.
Leans his hands on the animal's head before slaughtering it (סמיכה).

steps.whatToRemember: A נדבה is acceptable because its risk (מעילה) can be avoided, the way הלל did. A נדר's risk cannot be avoided this way.

phrases.english: [He can act] like Hillel the Elder.
As it is taught [in a baraita]:
They said about Hillel the Elder

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא מָעַל אָדָם בְּעוֹלָתוֹ כׇּל יָמָיו.
phrases.english: that no person misused his burnt offering all his days.
He would bring it while it was still unconsecrated to the Temple courtyard,
and consecrate it, lean his hands on it, and slaughter it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a practical method that removes the risk.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נדבה carries the same risk as a נדר.
steps.terutzMaskana: A נדבה's risk can be avoided by making the animal holy at the last moment, like הלל.

steps.title: What about voluntary נזירות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: הלל's method works for קרבנות, but how does a voluntary נזירות avoid risk?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for a נדבה of קרבנות. But for a נדבה of נזירות, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the answer for קרבנות but points out that it does not cover נזירות, which our משנה also mentions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נזירות cannot be taken on 'at the last moment' like הלל's offering. It lasts for a period of time, and the person might fail to keep its rules. So the risk seems to remain.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (for one case, but what about another?).
The state of being a נזיר.
What is there to say?

phrases.english: This works out well for a gift offering of sacrifices.
[But regarding] a voluntary acceptance of naziriteship,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of step 5 to קרבנות and challenges the case of נזירות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that every נדבה in our משנה is free of risk.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הלל's method only works for animals; a voluntary נזירות still risks being broken.

steps.title: רבי מאיר follows שמעון הצדיק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר holds like שמעון הצדיק about נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רבי מאיר) holds like שמעון הצדיק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short answer: about נזירות, רבי מאיר follows the view of שמעון הצדיק. It is setting up the next lines, which will explain that view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not yet say what שמעון הצדיק held. It only tells us that his approach is the key to why a voluntary נזירות can be acceptable for רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like (the view of) someone.
Shimon the Righteous, an early כהן גדול.

phrases.english: He holds like Shimon HaTzaddik.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the view to an earlier authority.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A voluntary נזירות seems risky, so רבי מאיר should discourage it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר follows שמעון הצדיק, whose view is explained next, so voluntary נזירות can fit his opinion.

steps.title: שמעון הצדיק's rule and his meeting with the handsome נזיר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: שמעון הצדיק never ate an impure נזיר's אשם except once. That time a handsome נזיר came from the South, and שמעון הצדיק asked him why he would destroy his beautiful hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: שמעון הצדיק said, 'In all my days I only ate the guilt-offering of an impure נזיר once. A נזיר came from the South. He had beautiful eyes, a handsome face, and curly locks. I asked him: My son, why would you destroy such beautiful hair?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא behind Step 7's claim that רבי מאיר holds like שמעון הצדיק about נזירות. This step sets up the story. We meet the young man, and שמעון הצדיק asks him a question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמעון הצדיק usually refused to eat this offering. That shows he did not approve of how most people became נזירים. The one exception is about to be explained, and it will show what kind of נזירות he did approve of.

keyTerms.meaning: As a ברייתא teaches (a teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה)
Shimon the Righteous, a כהן גדול from early in the second בית המקדש period
The guilt-offering a נזיר brings when he becomes impure during his נזירות
Locks of hair

phrases.english: As it is taught: Shimon HaTzaddik said:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. He is normally called just שמעון הצדיק.

phrases.english: In all my days I never ate
the guilt-offering of an impure nazir, except one.
One time a certain man came,
a nazir, from the South,
and I saw that he had beautiful eyes
and was good-looking,
and his locks were arranged in curls.
I said to him: My son,
what did you see that made you decide to destroy
this beautiful hair of yours?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that is the source for Step 7's claim that רבי מאיר follows שמעון הצדיק.
steps.raayaObject: Step 7's claim that רבי מאיר follows שמעון הצדיק, who praised a voluntary נזירות taken purely for the sake of Heaven
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of שמעון הצדיק and the נזיר from the South

steps.title: The shepherd explains why he became a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The young man explains what happened. He saw his reflection in a spring and felt his יצר הרע pulling him toward pride. He swore to shave his hair for the sake of Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: 'I was a shepherd for my father in my town. I went to draw water from the spring and looked at my reflection. My יצר suddenly rushed at me and tried to push me out of the world. I said to it: Wicked one! Why are you proud in a world that isn't yours, proud of a body that will one day be food for worms? I swear by the Temple service that I will shave you for Heaven!'
steps.whatsHappening: The young man answers שמעון הצדיק's question. He became a נזיר to fight his own vanity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His נזירות did not come from anger or a careless moment. It was a deliberate choice to break his pride. That is why his case is different from the others.

keyTerms.meaning: Reflection (in the water)
Inclination, here meaning the יצר הרע (the urge toward wrongdoing)
Worms and maggots (what the body becomes in the grave)
An oath: 'By the Temple service!'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: רוֹעֶה הָיִיתִי לְאַבָּא בְּעִירִי,
phrases.english: He said to me: I was a shepherd for my father in my town.
I went to draw water from the spring
and I looked at my reflection,
and my inclination suddenly rushed at me
and tried to drive me out of the world.
I said to it: Wicked one!
phrases.notes: He is talking to his own יצר, not to a person.

phrases.english: Why are you proud
in a world that is not yours,

phrases.aramaic: בְּמִי שֶׁהוּא עָתִיד לִהְיוֹת רִמָּה וְתוֹלֵעָה?
phrases.english: of one who will one day be worms and maggots?
phrases.notes: He means his own body, which will end up in the grave.

phrases.english: By the Temple service, I will shave you for Heaven!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לִי: רוֹעֶה הָיִיתִי לְאַבָּא בְּעִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שמעון הצדיק's question from Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the young man chose to become a נזיר and give up his beautiful hair
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He became a נזיר to defeat the pride he felt when he saw his reflection.

steps.title: שמעון הצדיק praises the young נזיר
steps.stepSummary: שמעון הצדיק kissed him on the head. He blessed him that there should be many נזירים like him and applied the פסוק about נזירות to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: I immediately stood up and kissed him on his head. I said: 'My son, may there be many people in ישראל who take נזירות like you. The פסוק speaks about you: "A man who clearly utters a vow of a נזיר, to set himself apart for ה׳."'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. שמעון הצדיק shows that this young man's נזירות was exactly what the תורה wants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes the proof for Step 7. Most נזירות made שמעון הצדיק uncomfortable, but נזירות done purely for Heaven earned his full praise. That matches רבי מאיר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who take on נזירות
Clearly expresses or sets apart (from the פסוק about a נזיר)
To separate oneself as a נזיר

steps.whatToRemember: שמעון הצדיק avoided ordinary נזירות. A נזירות taken purely to serve Heaven and break one's pride is the ideal the פסוק describes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the idea that נזירות is only fully praiseworthy when it comes from pure motives. רבי מאיר's view in our משנה builds on that idea.

phrases.english: Immediately I stood up and kissed him on his head.
I said to him: My son,
may there be many like you who take vows of naziriteship in Israel.
About you the verse says:
"When a man clearly utters a vow, the vow of a nazir,
to set himself apart for ה׳."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the young man's explanation in Step 9 and closes the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נזירות taken purely for Heaven, to break one's pride, is the praiseworthy נזירות the פסוק describes.

steps.title: רבי מני asks why only this אשם was avoided
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני challenges the ברייתא. If שמעון הצדיק avoided the impure נזיר's אשם because it comes from a sin, he should have avoided every אשם, since they all come from sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני challenges this: 'What is special about the impure נזיר's אשם that he wouldn't eat it? Is it because it comes for a sin? Then he shouldn't eat any אשמות, since they all come for sins!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני questions the reason behind שמעון הצדיק's practice. He suggests a reason and shows that it doesn't hold up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The obvious explanation is that שמעון הצדיק didn't want to eat an offering brought because of a sin. But almost every אשם is brought because of a sin, so that reason can't explain why he singled out the נזיר's אשם. The גמרא will need a different reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenges it strongly
An אמורא who raises the challenge
What is different about
Guilt-offerings

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מני is not disagreeing with the story. He is only showing that the simple reason, 'it comes for a sin,' cannot be the real reason for שמעון הצדיק's practice.

phrases.english: Rabbi Mani strongly objects to it:
What is different about the guilt-offering of an impure nazir
that he did not eat it?
Because it comes for a sin?
Then he should not eat any guilt-offerings either,
since they come for sin!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning behind שמעון הצדיק's practice described in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמעון הצדיק's practice of not eating the impure נזיר's אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason is that the offering comes because of a sin, the same reason applies to all אשמות. So singling out the נזיר's אשם makes no sense.

steps.title: רבי יונה explains the real concern: regret
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה answers that the concern is regret, not sin. An impure נזיר's days get longer, so he may regret his vow, and his offerings become like חולין in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונה said to him: This is the reason. When people regret their deeds, they become נזירים. When they become impure and their days of נזירות get longer, they regret having become נזירים. It turns out they are bringing חולין into the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונה answers רבי מני's question from step 11. He explains why שמעון הצדיק avoided only the impure נזיר's אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מני assumed the reason was that the אשם comes from a sin, which would cover every אשם. רבי יונה gives a different reason. An impure נזיר has to start his count over, so his term gets longer than he planned. He may then regret the whole נזירות, and offerings brought with regret are not really wanted, so they are like חולין brought into the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: They regret (here: people who feel sorry about something, which leads them to become נזירים)
The days of the נזיר's term
They regret (here: they feel sorry they became נזירים)
Non-sacred, ordinary items or animals
The courtyard of the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the word 'regret' appears twice with two different meanings. The first time (תוהין), the regret is what pushes the person to become a נזיר. The second time (מתחרטין), he regrets the נזירות itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer removes רבי מני's challenge. The problem belongs only to the impure נזיר, so שמעון הצדיק had no reason to avoid every אשם.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yona said to him:
This is the reason:
When they regret [their deeds], they become nazirites.
And when they become impure
and their days of naziriteship increase,
they regret them,
phrases.notes: He means they regret having become נזירים.

phrases.english: and it turns out they are bringing
non-sacred animals into the Temple courtyard.
phrases.notes: Since he doesn't really want to bring these offerings, it is as if they were never truly sacred.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹנָה, הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי מני's challenge from step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason that applies only to the impure נזיר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמעון הצדיק avoided the אשם because it comes from a sin, so he should have avoided every אשם
steps.terutzMaskana: The concern is that an impure נזיר may regret his longer נזירות, which makes his offerings like חולין

steps.title: Then a pure נזיר should be a problem too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יונה: if the worry is regret, a pure נזיר might also regret his vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even a pure נזיר should be a problem as well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יונה's answer. If regret is the problem, why did שמעון הצדיק eat a pure נזיר's offerings?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונה's reason seems to prove too much. Any נזיר could regret his נזירות, so the worry should also reach a pure נזיר's offerings. But step 8 said שמעון הצדיק avoided only the impure נזיר's אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (a common way of starting a challenge)
A נזיר who stayed pure and finished his term normally
Also, as well

phrases.english: If so,
then even a pure nazirite as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ נָזִיר טָהוֹר נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יונה's answer from step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יונה's reason that regret makes the offerings like חולין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The worry about regret should apply to a pure נזיר too, yet שמעון הצדיק ate a pure נזיר's offerings

steps.title: A pure נזיר measured himself before vowing
steps.stepSummary: A pure נזיר is not a concern. He judged his own strength before he vowed, and his term went as planned.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pure נזיר is not a concern, because he judged himself and saw that he was able to make this vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 13 and explains why a pure נזיר is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before vowing, a person estimates how long a נזירות he can handle. A pure נזיר keeps exactly the term he planned, so there is no reason to think he regrets it. An impure נזיר's term grows longer than he planned, and that extra time is what can lead to regret.

keyTerms.meaning: He measured himself, meaning he judged his own strength
To make a vow

steps.whatToRemember: שמעון הצדיק avoided only the impure נזיר's אשם. The reason is not sin. It is the fear that the longer term made him regret his נזירות, which would make his offerings like חולין.

phrases.english: A pure nazirite, no,
because he assessed himself
that he is able to vow.
phrases.notes: He knew he could keep the vow for the whole term, and the term did not get longer.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a difference between the two cases (pure versus impure נזיר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A pure נזיר might also regret his vow
steps.terutzMaskana: A pure נזיר judged his strength in advance and kept the term he planned, so there is no worry that he regrets it

steps.title: Introducing a second answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a different answer to the earlier question of which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to offer a second, different answer about whose opinion the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole discussion on this amud (steps 1–14) assumed that the משנה follows רבי מאיר. 'ואיבעית אימא' signals that the גמרא will now name a different תנא behind the משנה, as a second answer to that same question.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (a phrase that introduces a second answer)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It goes back to the question of whose view the משנה follows, which the גמרא answered with רבי מאיר. The actual second answer comes right after this line.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שמעון הצדיק discussion and goes back to the basic question of which תנא the משנה follows, to offer an answer other than רבי מאיר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces an alternative answer (the content follows)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה must follow רבי מאיר, with all the explanations given in steps 1–14
steps.terutzMaskana: There is a second possible way to identify whose view the משנה follows
